main finding: Mahalanobis feature distance is the strongest overall quantitative gatekeeper in the merged PR #21 comparison.
key metric/result: AUROC 0.9724, AUPRC 0.9975, FPR@95%TPR 0.2000, OOD recall at val-ID threshold 0.9079
dissertation implication: Use Mahalanobis as the primary binary FAF OOD gatekeeper baseline.
limitation: ID test set is synthetic fallback, not real clinical FAF validation.

main finding: Mahalanobis remains best under bootstrap uncertainty for AUROC and AUPRC and has the lowest FPR@95%TPR estimate.
dissertation implication: Ranking results are stable; threshold safety should be discussed more cautiously.
limitation: FPR@95%TPR confidence intervals are wider and overlap with Global feature kNN.

main finding: Mahalanobis is already strong at 50 ID images and saturates around 500 to 700 images.
key metric/result: AUROC rises from 0.9389 at 50 images to 0.9724 at 700 images.
dissertation implication: Feature-distance gating is data-efficient in this synthetic-backed proof of concept.
limitation: PatchCore memory-bank size was not varied in this sweep.

main finding: ID-calibrated Mahalanobis thresholds give the best deployment-style trade-off.
key metric/result: val_id_quantile_95: ID false rejection 0.0467, OOD recall 0.9079; fixed_id_rejection_20: ID false rejection 0.1200, OOD recall 0.9388
dissertation implication: Recommend validation-ID threshold calibration; use research 95% TPR only for evaluation.
limitation: Clinical threshold selection requires real FAF validation and operational cost targets.

main finding: Severity response is mixed: rectangle annotation, border crop, blur, and Gaussian noise are detectable, while text watermark and JPEG compression remain hard.
key metric/result: Best monotonic responses: Mahalanobis border_crop and Autoencoder rectangle_annotation Spearman 0.9685; hardest artifact family: text_watermark mean reject rate 0.0469
dissertation implication: Stress tests reveal both strengths and blind spots; do not claim universal monotonicity.
limitation: Generated artifacts are proof-of-concept stress tests, not clinical prevalence estimates.

main finding: Mahalanobis is correct while PatchCore L3 is wrong on many cases, but PatchCore catches many Mahalanobis text-watermark misses.
strongest method: Mahalanobis feature quantitatively; PatchCore L3 qualitatively
key metric/result: All methods correct 1195; Mahalanobis correct/PatchCore wrong 446; PatchCore catches 111 Mahalanobis false negatives
dissertation implication: Use Mahalanobis for decisions and PatchCore for localizable discussion examples.
limitation: Disagreement cases come from synthetic fallback ID and curated OOD stress examples.

main finding: Semantic outliers and modality shifts separate clearly from ID, while text watermark remains close to ID.
key metric/result: CIFAR centroid distance to ID 12.6234; OCT 7.2531; colour fundus 3.7114; text watermark 0.0811
dissertation implication: Global feature-space separation explains Mahalanobis strength and text-watermark weakness.
limitation: PCA is a 2D visualization of one feature family, not proof of clinical separability.

main finding: Mahalanobis gives the best performance/resource trade-off; PatchCore L3 adds localization at higher cost.
key metric/result: Mahalanobis: 6.2061 MB, 39.3631 ms/image, AUROC 0.9724; PatchCore L3: 16.0489 MB, 55.8631 ms/image, AUROC 0.8819
dissertation implication: Mahalanobis is practical for a prototype gatekeeper; PatchCore is useful as an explanation companion.
limitation: Runtime is a local smoke scoring measurement over 22 images; fit time was not remeasured.

main finding: Text watermark is the hardest Mahalanobis subtype and dominates false negatives.
strongest method: PatchCore L3 as complement for this failure mode
key metric/result: Mahalanobis text_watermark only-subtype AUROC 0.7361; 129/152 Mahalanobis false negatives are text watermark.
dissertation implication: Use false-negative and disagreement figures to motivate hybrid/localization future work.
limitation: Subtle local artifacts may remain underrepresented or synthetic relative to clinical acquisition failures.
